If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM()` fails likely due to an infinite loop or otherwise incorrect behavior in the `asPath()` method on a DOM node with a reset default namespace (empty namespace URI). The current bug report indicates that calling `.asPath()` on a node within an XML snippet where an element resets the default namespace (`xmlns=""`) causes a serious endless loop.

The analyzed `DOMNodePointer.asPath()` method constructs the XPath by recursively calling `asPath()` on the parent pointer and then appending a path segment for the current node. For element nodes, it relies on namespace URI and prefix information obtained from `getNamespaceURI()` and the `NamespaceResolver` to construct a qualified name prefix for XPath segments.

The namespace URI retrieval (`getNamespaceURI()`) ultimately calls the static method `getNamespaceURI(Node)`. That method gets the namespace URI from the node's element itself. If that's null, it attempts to fetch it manually by looking up namespace declarations (xmlns attributes) walking up the ancestor chain. If it fails to find a namespace URI, it returns `null`.

The `matchesQName(Node n)` helper method used by `getRelativePositionByQName()` compares nodes based on matching namespace URIs and local names if the namespace URI for the node is not null; otherwise, it falls back to comparing node names.

The failure likely arises because the "test" element in the test XML resets the default namespace to an empty string (`xmlns=""`) meaning it effectively has no namespace URI. When `getNamespaceURI` returns `null` or an empty string, the `asPath()` method's logic attempts to find a prefix for the namespace via the `NamespaceResolver` (which might be default or inherited) and might fail to obtain a proper prefix.

This missing or default namespace prefix leads to incorrect path segment construction in the `asPath()` method, triggering it to fall into the `else` branch where it appends `"node()"` plus an index based on element position for nodes with no prefix. During this recursion, the path calculation may repeatedly try to identify relative positions by QName between nodes failing on namespace URI resolution due to the reset default namespace.

The critical problem is the treatment of nodes with reset or empty default namespaces, causing an infinite recursion or endless loop in `asPath()` because no valid prefix or namespace URI is resolved, and the code repeatedly falls back to trying to compute relative positions in a way that never resolves properly.

In summary:
- The "test" element having `xmlns=""` results in an empty or null namespace URI.
- `asPath()` depends on namespace URI and prefixes to build path segments.
- Failure to resolve a proper prefix causes fallback to `node()` with relative position.
- The recursive calls for relative position may loop or behave incorrectly due to namespace resolution mishandling.
- This leads to the serious endless loop when requesting `.asPath()` on that node.

This diagnosis aligns with the current bug report's sample XML and problem description. The root cause is the handling of reset default namespace elements when constructing XPath strings via `asPath()`.

Potential fix strategies involve ensuring that empty or reset namespaces are properly handled in namespace URI and prefix resolution when building the XPath, preventing infinite recursions or misuse of relative position logic.

Hence, the bug is primarily located in the `DOMNodePointer.asPath()` method and involved namespace resolution helpers (`getNamespaceURI`, `getPrefix`) that contribute to prefix determination.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
